s: What is the main aim of The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024?
o: To give constitutional status and protection to cooperative societies
Simultaneous elections in Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies
To abolish Election Tribunals in India and enable the trial of election petitions by High Courts
To confer a constitutional status to National Commission for Backward Classes

s: On simultaneous elections, which body–year–view pair is correctly matched?
x: The Law Commission’s 170th Report (1999) supported simultaneous elections; the EC was 1983, the Standing Committee 2015 and NITI Aayog 2017.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about proposals linked to simultaneous elections?
o: The 2018 Law Commission draft proposed a constructive no-confidence motion
The constructive no-confidence motion is borrowed from the United Kingdom
The Kovind Committee proposed a phased model of simultaneous elections
The Kovind Committee proposed local-body polls within 100 days of Lok Sabha and Assembly polls
x: The constructive no-confidence motion is borrowed from Germany, not the United Kingdom.

s: Under the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, elections to local bodies are conducted by which institutions?
x: The 73rd and 74th Amendments provide for local elections through State Election Commissions. The Election Commission of India and the other institutions listed are not the bodies specified for this function.

s: What was the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 formed mainly to examine?
x: The JPC chaired by P.P. Chaudhary examined the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, concerning simultaneous elections. The Bill was introduced on 17 December 2024.

s: Who chaired the High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections (One Nation One Election), 2023-24?
x: Former President Ram Nath Kovind chaired the High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections. P.P. Chaudhary chairs the JPC on the resulting 129th Amendment Bill; Dinesh Goswami (1990) and Indrajit Gupta (1998) chaired earlier committees on electoral reform.

s: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 proposes to insert which Article and amend which Articles to provide the constitutional framework for simultaneous elections?
o: Insert Article 80A and amend Articles 81 and 170
Insert Article 83A and amend Articles 82 and 173
Insert Article 82A and amend Articles 83 and 172
Insert Article 324A and amend Articles 85 and 174
x: The Bill inserts Article 82A and amends Articles 83 and 172. The other options mention Articles that are not identified in the Bill’s stated constitutional changes.

s: The companion legislation to the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 concerns which Union Territories?
o: Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Chandigarh
Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir
x: The companion Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024 concerns Delhi, Puducherry and J&K; local bodies are excluded from the 129th Amendment Bill.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024?
o: The President notifies the appointed date.
The Election Commission notifies the appointed date.
After a mid-term dissolution, elections are held only for the unexpired term.
x: The appointed date is notified by the President, not the Election Commission.

s: Up to the last week of which session was the term of the Joint Parliamentary Committee on simultaneous elections extended?
x: The JPC's term was extended to the last week of the Monsoon Session of 2026; its report was still pending.

s: In the context of concerns surrounding simultaneous elections, which principles did Kesavananda Bharati identify as part of the basic structure?
o: Free and fair elections and parliamentary democracy
x: Kesavananda Bharati identified free and fair elections and parliamentary democracy as part of the basic structure. The other pairs are not the principles specified in this context.

s: Which Law Commission report (1999) supported simultaneous elections?
x: The Law Commission's 170th Report (1999), under Justice B.P. Jeevan Reddy, supported simultaneous elections.

s: Under which Justice was the Law Commission's 170th Report (1999) on simultaneous elections given?
x: Justice B.P. Jeevan Reddy headed the Law Commission that gave the 170th Report.

s: The Kovind High-Level Committee recommended local body elections within how many days of the simultaneous polls?
x: The Kovind Committee (2023-24) recommended a phased model with local body polls within 100 days.

s: Which Constitution Amendment Bill, proposing 850 Lok Sabha seats, was defeated?
x: The 131st Amendment Bill (850 seats) was defeated; the 129th is the ONOE Bill.

s: From which country is the 'constructive no-confidence motion', suggested in the 2018 Law Commission draft, borrowed?
x: The constructive no-confidence motion is borrowed from Germany.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024:
1. It inserts Article 82A.
2. It amends Articles 83 and 172.
3. It covers elections to local bodies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: local bodies are excluded from the Bill.

s: Who is the chairman of the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024?
x: The JPC on the One Nation One Election Bill is chaired by P.P. Chaudhary.

s: Who chaired the 1990 committee on electoral reforms?
x: The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) was an earlier committee on electoral reforms; Indrajit Gupta's came in 1998.

s: In which year was the Fourth Lok Sabha dissolved early, after which simultaneous elections were not held again?
x: The Fourth Lok Sabha was dissolved in 1970 and fresh elections were held in 1971.

s: The Indrajit Gupta Committee of 1998 is associated with which subject?
x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) was an electoral-reform committee, like the earlier Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990).

s: In which year were elections to the Lok Sabha and all State Assemblies last held together before the cycle broke?
x: Simultaneous elections were held in 1952, 1957, 1962 and 1967; the cycle broke in 1968-69.

s: In which year did the Election Commission recommend a return to simultaneous elections?
x: The Election Commission recommended a return to simultaneous elections in 1983; the Law Commission's 170th Report followed in 1999.

s: According to the CMS, what was the approximate cost of the 2024 Lok Sabha election?
x: The Centre for Media Studies put the 2024 election cost at about ₹1.35 lakh crore, against ₹60,000 crore in 2019.

s: What does the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) provide in the notified-disaster framework?
o: The primary State fund for notified disasters
Additional aid for disasters of severe nature
Funds for long-term mitigation projects only
A fund financed solely by the States
x: The NDRF gives additional aid for severe disasters; the SDRF is the primary State fund for notified disasters.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the notified-disaster framework for 2026–2031?
o: The MHA is the nodal ministry for the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
The SDRF is the main State fund, with Centre and State contributions.
The NDRF gives additional aid for disasters of severe nature.
The notified calamities rose from 12 to 13.
x: Heatwave and lightning were both added, so the list rose from 12 to 14, not 13.

s: On the advice of the 16th Finance Commission, which of the following were added as notified disasters in August 2026?
x: Heatwave and lightning were added as notified disasters on 16th FC advice (Aug 2026). The other pairs are not what the 16th FC recommendation added.

s: What is the award period of the 16th Finance Commission?
x: The 16th FC, chaired by Arvind Panagariya, covers 2026-27 to 2030-31.

s: Under which Article is the Finance Commission a constitutional body?
x: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280; Article 148 deals with the CAG.

s: With heatwave and lightning added under the SDRF/NDRF guidelines for 2026-2031, to how many did the number of notified natural calamities rise from 12?
x: Adding heatwave and lightning raised the notified calamities from 12 to 14; victims receive relief under SDRF/NDRF norms.

s: Who is the chairman of the 16th Finance Commission?
x: The 16th Finance Commission (Article 280), award 2026-27 to 2030-31, is chaired by Arvind Panagariya.

s: What share of the divisible pool of central taxes did the 16th Finance Commission keep for the States?
x: The 16th Finance Commission kept the States' share at 41%.

s: Which prison-reform measure pair is correctly matched?
o: Model Prisons and Correctional Services Act – 2023
Support to Poor Prisoners Scheme – Digital prison initiative
x: The Model Prisons and Correctional Services Act is of 2023; the Model Prison Manual is of 2016 and E-Prisons is the digital initiative.

s: The Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir separates India from which country?
x: The LoC is the India–Pakistan line in J&K; the LAC denotes the India–China boundary.

s: Under which ministry does the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) function?
x: I4C is under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

s: According to Prison Statistics India 2024, which State or Union Territory recorded the highest prison occupancy rate?
x: Delhi recorded the highest prison occupancy rate in 2024, at 194.6%. Meghalaya, Jammu and Kashmir, and Madhya Pradesh also recorded high occupancy, but their rates were 163.5%, 148.3%, and 147.1% respectively.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about prison data and related legal provisions?
o: Delhi and Bihar had an undertrial share above 87%
Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar was decided in 1979
Sunil Batra v. Delhi Administration affirmed that prisoners retain fundamental rights
Under Section 479 of BNSS, a first-time offender is eligible for release on bond after one-half of the maximum sentence
x: Section 479 of the BNSS allows release of a first-time offender after one-third, not one-half, of the maximum sentence.

s: Under Section 479 of BNSS 2023, a first-time offender may be released on bond after serving what part of the maximum sentence?
x: A first-time offender who has served one-third of the maximum sentence may be released on bond, with the jail superintendent required to apply.

s: What was the key legal principle associated with the Supreme Court’s decision in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar?
o: It permits unnecessary arrests in all cases
It concerns the preparation of electoral rolls
x: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar is associated with discouraging unnecessary arrests. The tempting opposite option is incorrect because the ruling sought to prevent, rather than permit, unnecessary arrests.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the CAG audit of amenities at railway stations?
o: The CAG is appointed by Parliament
Testing was not as per norms at 59 stations in six railway zones
E. coli was found at stations including Hyderabad
The audit was tabled on 12 August 2026
x: The CAG is appointed by the President, not by Parliament.

s: Which State ranked first nationally in cybercrime control, victim services and digital platforms in the PMO-led PRAGATI review?
x: Telangana ranked first in the PRAGATI review; Sahyog and Samanvaya are portals and I4C is the coordination centre.

s: What was the national prison occupancy rate as per Prison Statistics India 2024?
x: Occupancy was 112.7%, a decade-low; Delhi had the highest at 194.6%.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Prison Statistics India 2024?
o: The occupancy rate of 112.7% was a decade-low.
Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest occupancy rate.
x: Delhi, at 194.6%, recorded the highest occupancy, not Uttar Pradesh.

s: Who releases the PLFS monthly bulletin?
x: PLFS is released by the National Statistics Office under MoSPI.

s: What was the overall unemployment rate (15+) as per the PLFS July 2026 bulletin?
x: UR fell to 5.1% from 5.5% in June; rural UR was 4.5% and urban about 6.7%.

s: Which Telangana-used portal recorded 89.41% content-takedown success in the PRAGATI cybercrime review?
x: Sahyog recorded 89.41% takedown success; Samanvaya resolved 96.68% of inter-State requests.

s: The CAG holds office for six years or up to what age?
x: The CAG (Article 148) is appointed by the President for 6 years or until 65 years of age.

s: Which body released Prison Statistics India 2024, which showed a decade-low occupancy rate of 112.7%?
o: Bureau of Police Research and Development
x: Prison Statistics India is published by the NCRB under the MHA.

s: On which approach are the monthly PLFS estimates, introduced from January 2025, based?
x: From January 2025 the PLFS gives monthly and quarterly estimates on the Current Weekly Status approach.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
x: The CAG is a constitutional authority under Article 148, appointed by the President.

s: What was the overall Labour Force Participation Rate (15+) as per the PLFS July 2026 bulletin?
x: The July 2026 PLFS bulletin put overall LFPR at 55.4% (up from 54.4%); WPR was 52.5% and female LFPR 34.4%.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for free legal aid?
x: Article 39A, a Directive Principle, provides for equal justice and free legal aid.

s: For whom is the TG-Veer portal launched by Telangana DGP C.V. Anand meant?
x: TG-Veer is a single-window grievance portal for families of police martyrs, with QR-code family cards.

s: As per Prison Statistics India 2024, about what share of prison inmates are undertrials?
x: Undertrials are about 73% of inmates; convicts fell to 26.6% in 2024.

src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: Yashoda AI Initiative to enhance women's AI and Cybersecurity skills was launched by
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2026 changes at the Ministry of Education?
o: Pralhad Joshi was given additional charge of the Ministry.
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Education Minister.
MHRD was renamed the Ministry of Education in 2015.
The Ministry was called the Ministry of Human Resource Development until 2020.
x: MHRD was renamed the Ministry of Education in 2020, not 2015.

s: According to the August 2026 constitutional update, who was the Chief Justice of India?
x: Justice Surya Kant was the Chief Justice of India in the stated update. Justice R. Subhash Reddy was identified as the chair of the committee on the SJP protests, while Raj Kumar Goyal and C.V. Anand held different positions.

s: In which year was the National Commission for Women established?
x: The NCW was established in 1992 under the NCW Act, 1990; its initiatives include Yashoda AI and She Serves.

s: Who was appointed Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities on July 16, 2026?
x: Harjit Singh Grewal was appointed Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities on July 16, 2026. Pralhad Joshi received additional charge of the Ministry of Education, while Justices B. V. Nagarathna and J. K. Maheshwari are associated with the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee appointments.

s: Which of the following communities is among the six notified minorities under the National Commission for Minorities?
x: The six notified minorities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains.

s: What is the nature of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Executive body set up by a Cabinet resolution
Statutory body under the NCM Act, 1992
x: The NCM is statutory under the NCM Act, 1992; the NCST is constitutional under Article 338A.

s: Which of the following pairs (body – nature) is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Law Commission is an executive body, neither constitutional nor statutory; the other pairs are correct.

s: Who was appointed Chairperson of the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee in 2026?
x: CJI Surya Kant appointed Justice B.V. Nagarathna, succeeding Justice J.K. Maheshwari.

s: Who chairs the National Commission for Women?
x: Vijaya Rahatkar chairs the NCW, a statutory body under the NCW Act, 1990.

s: Who launched AppCOMS 2.0 as Chief Information Commissioner?
x: CIC Raj Kumar Goyal launched AppCOMS 2.0, upgrading the original AppCOMS of 2016.

s: Which body launched 'Yashoda AI' for AI awareness and digital literacy among women?
x: The NCW (chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar) launched Yashoda AI and She Serves at Jalandhar.

s: Which is the nodal department for the Central Information Commission?
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
x: The CIC, a statutory body set up in 2005 under the RTI Act, has DoPT as its nodal department.

s: The 'She Serves' initiative of the National Commission for Women promotes careers for young women in which field?
x: NCW's 'She Serves' promotes careers in the Armed Forces for young women; 'Yashoda AI' is on AI literacy.

s: Under which Act is the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee constituted?
x: The Supreme Court Legal Services Committee is set up under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

s: Who chairs the Supreme Court committee on the SJP protests over NEET and police action?
x: The five-member committee is chaired by Justice R. Subhash Reddy; Justice R.K. Jha is a member.

s: The Empowered Committee for the PM Research Chair (PMRC), intended to attract Indian-origin researchers to priority sectors, is chaired by whom?
x: The Empowered Committee for the PM Research Chair, a Ministry of Education scheme to attract Indian-origin researchers in 13 priority sectors, is chaired by Principal Scientific Adviser Ajay Kumar Sood.

s:
Consider the following statements about SEBI's expert working group on debenture trustees (June 2026):
1. It is chaired by former SEBI Whole Time Member Ananta Barua.
2. Former SBI Chairman Rajnish Kumar is its co-chair.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct; the group reviews the SEBI (Debenture Trustees) Regulations, 1993, including net-worth requirements.

s: The PM Research Chair scheme of the Ministry of Education covers how many priority sectors?
x: PMRC targets Indian-origin researchers in 13 priority sectors; its Empowered Committee is chaired by PSA Ajay Kumar Sood.

s: Under MHA rules, no new solar, wind or hybrid project can be set up within what distance of the LoC, LAC or IB?
x: New projects are banned within 1 km; the 50 km zone needs prior security clearance, not an outright ban.

s: Under MHA rules, a new renewable-energy project within what distance of the International Border needs a Ministry of Defence NOC?
x: Projects within 20 km of the International Border require a Ministry of Defence NOC.

s: Which company will implement the 250 MW solar-plus-BESS project on former cantonment land at Sitapur, Uttar Pradesh?
x: NTPC will implement the 250 MW solar and BESS project on about 850 acres at Sitapur.

s: The Civil Defence Volunteer Force announced from the Red Fort is governed by the Civil Defence Act of which year?
x: The relevant law is the Civil Defence Act, 1968 with the Civil Defence Rules, 1968; MHA is the nodal ministry.

s: Which force has been designated the Recognized Security Organization for port security audits and training?
x: CISF is the Recognized Security Organization; the proposed Bureau of Port Security will handle physical and cyber security of ports and ships.

s: The proposed Bureau of Port Security is modelled on which organisation and placed under which ministry?
o: BCAS; Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
CISF; Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
x: The Bureau of Port Security is modelled on BCAS and is to function under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. CISF is the designated Recognized Security Organization for port-security audits and training, while BCAS is under the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

s: Which agency conducted Operation Chakra-6 (June 2026) against digital arrest scams?
x: Operation Chakra–6 was a CBI operation against digital arrest scams.

s: What do renewable-energy projects in the 50 km zone from the LoC, LAC or IB need under MHA rules?
o: A Ministry of Defence NOC only
x: The 50 km zone needs prior security clearance; the ban applies only within 1 km and the MoD NOC within 20 km of the IB.

s: For the security of which pilgrimage was Operation Shiva 2026 of the Indian Army conducted?
x: Operation Shiva secured the Amarnath Yatra 2026, using counter-drone and EW systems for the first time.

s: In which year was the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security, on which the Bureau of Port Security is modelled, set up?
x: BCAS was set up in 1987 under the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

s: Which body developed the Abhigyan police app linked to NAFIS?
x: The Abhigyan app, linked to NAFIS for fingerprint matching, was developed by the NCRB (est. 1986).

s: In which year was the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) established?
x: The CBI was set up in 1963; the NCRB came later, in 1986.

s: Who is the Director of the CBI, the agency behind Operation Chakra-6 against digital arrest scams?
x: The CBI, set up in 1963, is headed by Director Praveen Sood.

s: NITI Aayog's Ayurveda roadmap identifies which system as Ayurveda's main global competitor?
x: Traditional Chinese Medicine is identified as Ayurveda's main competitor; Unani is still part of the Ministry of AYUSH.

s: Which report on the internationalisation of Ayurveda was released by NITI Aayog on 2 July 2026?
o: Strategic Roadmap for Making Ayurveda Global
x: The report released by NITI Aayog on 2 July 2026 was titled “Strategic Roadmap for Making Ayurveda Global.” The Global Ayurveda Register, Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia Export Edition and Global Information Portal are measures listed under the short-term phase, not the report title.

s: Who released the Strategic Roadmap for Making Ayurveda Global, which covers education, research, regulation, insurance, branding and medical value travel?
x: It is NITI Aayog's roadmap, and it goes beyond exports to cover education, research, regulation, insurance, branding and medical value travel.

s: The three pillars of NITI Aayog's Strategic Roadmap for Making Ayurveda Global are Availability, Acceptability and which other?
x: The pillars are Availability, Acceptability and Propagation, in a phased strategy up to 2047.

s: In NITI Aayog's Strategic Roadmap for Making Ayurveda Global, modernising the TKDL falls in which phase?
x: Modernising TKDL and Medical Value Travel hubs are medium-term measures; the Global Ayurveda Register is short-term.

s: Where is the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre located?
x: The WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre is in Jamnagar, Gujarat.

s: Which traditional medicine systems are included in the ICD-11 Traditional Medicine module, with interventions coded under ICHI?
o: Ayurveda, Siddha and Traditional Chinese Medicine
x: The ICD-11 Traditional Medicine module includes Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani, and their interventions are coded under ICHI. Sowa-Rigpa and Traditional Chinese Medicine are not part of the stated combination.

s: In which year was Sowa-Rigpa (Amchi), the traditional medicine system of the Himalayan region, recognised?
x: Sowa-Rigpa was recognised in 2010; Siddha is associated with Tamil Nadu.

s: Ayurveda and herbal exports reached what value in 2023?
x: Exports rose from USD 1.09 bn (2014) to USD 2.16 bn (2023).

s: Who chairs the Mission Steering Group under the Ayurveda roadmap?
x: The short-term Mission Steering Group is chaired by the Minister of Ayush.

s: Which ancient text is associated with surgery, earning its author the title 'Father of Surgery'?
x: The Sushruta Samhita deals with surgery; Sushruta is called the Father of Surgery.

s: Under NITI Aayog's Ayurveda roadmap, integration of Ayurveda into at least how many national health systems is targeted by 2047?
x: The long-term phase (up to 2047) targets integration in at least 20 national health systems and insurance in at least 10 countries.

s: With which State is the Siddha system of medicine mainly associated?
x: Siddha is the traditional medicine system of Tamil Nadu; Sowa-Rigpa belongs to the Himalayan region.

s: Which Article deals with the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
x: Article 338A deals with the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes; Article 342 concerns identification of Scheduled Tribes.

s: What is the name of India's first permanent independent research centre on transport economics established at New Delhi?
o: National Council of Applied Economic Research
Centre for Transport, Mobility and Logistics Economics
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
x: The Centre for Transport, Mobility and Logistics Economics, New Delhi, is India's first permanent independent research centre on transport economics. The National Highways Authority of India, National Council of Applied Economic Research and Ministry of Road Transport and Highways are related institutions or authorities, but they are not the name of this centre.

s: Samadhan Didi, the first AI voice chatbot for CPGRAMS, supports how many Eighth Schedule languages?
x: Samadhan Didi, developed by DARPG with Bhashini, supports all 22 Eighth Schedule languages.

s:
Assertion (A): Pension Sahayak is an AI grievance portal developed by DARPG.
Reason (R): Pension Sahayak provides access in 22 languages through Bhashini.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Assertion A is false because Pension Sahayak is the PFRDA AI grievance portal, not a DARPG portal. Reason R is true: it provides grievance access in 22 languages through Bhashini.

s: Sarvam AI, the first full-stack indigenous AI unicorn, is India's which unicorn?
x: Sarvam AI became India's 130th unicorn and the 5th of 2026.

s: Who launched the Jago AI Assistant on ST welfare schemes?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: Jago AI Assistant is by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, in English and Hindi.

s: Which department developed Samadhan Didi, the first AI voice chatbot for CPGRAMS, with Bhashini?
x: Samadhan Didi was built by DARPG with Bhashini and works in all 22 Eighth Schedule languages.

s: Who are the founders of Sarvam AI, India's first full-stack indigenous AI unicorn?
x: Sarvam AI (Bengaluru, 2023) was founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the identification of Scheduled Tribes?
x: Under Article 342 the President specifies the Scheduled Tribes; Article 338A deals with the NCST.

s: The Vyomaa Innovation Challenge for offline multilingual voice AI was launched by which body?
x: Bhashini ran the Vyomaa Innovation Challenge with Current AI and Kalpa Impact; its device is 'Sunno Sutra'.

s: Which of the following statements about the PCPNDT Act and ultrasound machines is incorrect?
o: The law was enacted in 1994 as the Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Act.
A machine may be used at any location after it has been registered once.
Registration is required before purchasing ultrasound machines.
The 2003 amendment added pre-conception provisions and renamed it the PCPNDT (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act.
x: The incorrect statement is that a registered machine may be used at any location. The machine must stay at its registered location; registration is required before purchase and sex disclosure is prohibited.

s: Which of the following statements about India's first indigenous African Swine Fever vaccine is incorrect?
o: African Swine Fever is a viral disease of pigs that infects humans.
It was developed by ICAR–NIHSAD, Bhopal.
It was dedicated by Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
It is the MA-104 Cell Line-Based Live Attenuated African Swine Fever Vaccine.
x: The incorrect statement is that African Swine Fever infects humans; the disease does not infect humans. The vaccine was developed by ICAR–NIHSAD, Bhopal, and was dedicated by Shivraj Singh Chouhan.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the FSSAI action against misleading food claims is incorrect?
o: FSSAI issued more than 150 notices concerning misleading advertisements, false claims and labelling.
In May 2025, FSSAI advised stopping the use of the expression “Energy Drink” on labels.
Mondelez India withdrew health and nutrient-comparison claims on Bournvita.
The action covered labels, advertisements, e-commerce listings and delivery platforms.
x: The second statement is incorrect: in May 2025 FSSAI advised stopping the use of "100%" on labels, not "Energy Drink". The other statements are correct: FSSAI issued 150+ notices covering labels, ads, e-commerce listings and delivery platforms, and Mondelez India withdrew health and nutrient-comparison claims on Bournvita.

s: Which institute developed India's first indigenous African Swine Fever vaccine?
x: The MA-104 cell-line vaccine was developed by ICAR-NIHSAD, Bhopal; ASF does not infect humans.

s: In which year was the Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act enacted, later renamed the PCPNDT Act by a 2003 amendment?
x: The PNDT Act was enacted in 1994; the 2003 amendment added pre-conception techniques and renamed it the PCPNDT Act.

src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
s: Which of the following religions has the largest global following across the world?
The High-Level Committee on demographic change linked to illegal immigration and other abnormal reasons was constituted by which authority?
x: The committee was constituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs to study demographic changes arising from illegal immigration and other abnormal reasons. The Inter-State Council and Finance Commission are separate constitutional bodies, while the Census Commissioner is a member of the committee.

s: In which case (2005) was illegal migration into Assam characterised as 'external aggression'?
x: The Sarbananda Sonowal case (2005) characterised illegal migration into Assam as external aggression.

s: The Madhukar Gupta Committee of 2016 is associated with which of the following?
o: The Union’s duty to protect States from external aggression
Protection of tribal land in the Santhal Pargana region
x: The Madhukar Gupta Committee of 2016 was associated with the Comprehensive Integrated Border Management System (CIBMS). The Assam Accord, tribal land protection and the Union’s protective duty arise from different legal or policy references.

s: To what level does the Education to Employment and Enterprise Standing Committee aim to raise India's share in the global services market by 2047?
x: The committee's goal is a 10% share in the global services market by 2047.

s: How many empowered teams did the Prime Minister announce on March 24, 2026, after a CCS review?
x: The Prime Minister announced seven empowered teams on March 24, 2026, following a CCS review.

s: Who chaired the High-Level Committee on Demographic Change proposed in May 2026?
x: The High-Level Committee on Demographic Change was chaired by Justice Prakash Prabhakar Navlekar and dealt with demographic change arising from illegal immigration.

s: Which Article of the Constitution places a duty on the Union to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance?
x: Article 355 sets the Union's duty to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance.

s: Who chairs the Education to Employment and Enterprise Standing Committee?
x: NITI Aayog CEO Nidhi Chhibber chairs it; its first meeting was on 22 May 2026.

s: Within what period must the High-Level Committee on demographic change submit its report?
x: The report is due within 1 year, extendable by 6 months.

s: What did the Lt. Gen. S.K. Sinha Report (1998) deal with?
o: Demographic change in border districts due to illegal migration
x: The S.K. Sinha Report (1998) flagged demographic change in border districts caused by illegal migration.

s: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955 relates to which of the following?
o: National Register of Citizens in all States
x: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955 was inserted to give effect to the Assam Accord.

s: What was India's Total Fertility Rate as per NFHS-5?
x: NFHS-5 put India's TFR at 2.0, cited in the context of the demographic change committee.

s: The K.G. Balakrishnan Commission (October 2022) examines extending SC status to Dalits converted to which religions?
x: The Commission examines SC status for Dalits who converted to Christianity and Islam.

s: Under Article 341, who specifies the Scheduled Castes for each State or Union Territory after consultation with the Governor?
o: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The President specifies the Scheduled Castes for each State or Union Territory after consulting the Governor. The SC list can be modified only by Parliament, so Parliament is not the authority that initially specifies it.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about reservation for Scheduled Castes?
o: Under Article 341, the President specifies SCs after consulting the Governor
The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 was originally for Hindus and later extended to Sikhs and Buddhists
Articles 330 and 332 provide reservation in legislatures
Reservation is provided for SCs in private-sector jobs
x: There is no reservation in private-sector jobs; the other three statements are correct.

s: Under Article 341, who alone can modify the list of Scheduled Castes?
x: The President notifies the SC list after consulting the Governor, but only Parliament can change it.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950:
1. It originally covered Hindus only.
2. It was extended to Sikhs in 1956.
3. It was extended to Christians in 1990.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1990 extension was to Buddhists; Christians and Muslims are not included.

s: The K.G. Balakrishnan Commission was notified by which ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The Commission of Inquiry was notified by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

s: Who was the first Dalit Chief Justice of India?
x: K.G. Balakrishnan, the 37th CJI (2007-2010), was the first Dalit CJI; he now heads the commission on SC status of converts.

s: Who heads the Commission of Inquiry on extending Scheduled Caste status to Dalits who converted to Christianity and Islam?
x: The commission set up on 6 October 2022 is headed by former CJI K.G. Balakrishnan, India's first Dalit CJI.

s: Who heads the Lok Sabha Estimates Committee for 2026–27?
x: Dr. Sanjay Jaiswal heads the Estimates Committee; K.C. Venugopal heads the PAC.

s: Regarding parliamentary committees, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Estimates Committee – 22 members, 15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha
Public Accounts Committee – Examines CAG reports
Committee on Public Undertakings – 30 members, Lok Sabha only
Committee on Privileges – Examines CAG reports
x: The PAC examines CAG reports; the Estimates Committee has 30 Lok Sabha members and the Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 (15 LS + 7 RS).

s: Who chairs the Public Accounts Committee for 2026-27?
x: K.C. Venugopal is the chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee for 2026–27, which examines CAG audit reports.

s: Who instituted the Sansad Ratna Awards?
x: The Sansad Ratna Awards were instituted by the Prime Point Foundation; the 2026 edition honoured 12 MPs.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Vice-President and the Rajya Sabha?
o: The Vice-President is the ex officio Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Article 63 provides for a Vice-President of India
The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members
x: The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, not the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

s: The Lok Sabha Estimates Committee for 2026-27 has how many members?
x: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from Lok Sabha; PAC and COPU have 22 (15 + 7).

s: Which of the following pairs (committee – members) is correctly matched?
o: Committee on Public Undertakings – 30, Lok Sabha only
Welfare of SCs and STs – 22 (15 LS + 7 RS)
x: PAC and COPU have 22 (15 + 7); the Estimates Committee has 30 from Lok Sabha only; the SC/ST Welfare Committee has 30 (20 + 10).

s: Who chairs the Lok Sabha Committee on Privileges, the first under the 18th Lok Sabha?
x: Ravi Shankar Prasad chairs the Committee on Privileges with 14 other MPs.

s: Who chairs the Joint Committee on the Corporate Laws Amendment Bill, 2026?
x: The Joint Committee on the Corporate Laws Amendment Bill, 2026 is chaired by Sudheer Gupta.

s: Who chairs the Lok Sabha Committee on Empowerment of Women constituted on 21 April 2026?
x: D. Purandeswari chairs the Committee on Empowerment of Women.

s: Who chairs the Rajya Sabha Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment, Forests and Climate Change from May 2026?
x: Medha Vishram Kulkarni was made its chair from 18 May 2026 under Rule 269.

s: Who chairs the Parliamentary Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes for 2026-27?
x: Faggan Singh Kulaste chairs the 30-member (20 LS + 10 RS) committee on Welfare of SCs and STs.

s: Who is the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha House Committee?
x: Dr. K. Laxman chairs the Rajya Sabha House Committee, which handles members' accommodation and amenities.

s: Who chairs the Telangana Women’s Commission, which has a five-year term?
x: Gadwal Vijayalakshmi, formerly the GHMC Mayor, is the Chair of the Telangana Women’s Commission, whose term is five years. Vijaya Rahatkar chairs the NCW, Annapurna Devi is the WCD Minister, and Kasoju Shankaramma is a member of the Telangana commission.

s: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body under which Article?
x: The NCSC is under Article 338; the 89th Amendment (2003) split it from the NCST and the 65th Amendment (1990) made it multi-member.

s: The NCBC received constitutional status under Article 338B through which Amendment?
x: The NCBC became statutory in 1993 and constitutional in 2018 under Article 338B (102nd Amendment).

s: Which body was replaced by the National Dental Commission set up on 19 March 2026?
x: The National Dental Commission replaced the Dental Council of India, established in 1949.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment split the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into separate NCSC and NCST?
x: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the combined commission, creating separate constitutional commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

s: Who assumed office as Chairperson of the NCBC on 27 March 2026?
x: Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti replaced Hans Raj Gangaram Ahir as NCBC Chairperson.

s: Who was appointed Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog in April 2026?
x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri replaced Suman Bery on 25 April 2026 and took charge on 8 May 2026.

s: Which of the following is an executive body, neither constitutional nor statutory?
x: The Law Commission is executive and advisory; NCSC, NCBC and the Finance Commission are constitutional.

s: Which Act was repealed when the National Dental Commission was set up in March 2026?
x: The National Dental Commission replaced the Dental Council of India and the Dentists Act, 1948 was repealed.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment made the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes a multi-member body?
x: The 65th Amendment (1990) made it multi-member; the 89th (2003) split it into NCSC and NCST.

s: Which factor is the 16th Finance Commission said to give weight to?
x: The 16th Finance Commission gives weight to contribution to GDP. The other options are demands for special constitutional or fiscal treatment mentioned in the federalism debate, not the stated criterion of the 16th Finance Commission.

s: Which of the following pairs consists of commissions on Centre-State relations?
o: Punchhi and All India Services Commission
x: The Sarkaria Commission and the Punchhi Commission are identified as commissions on Centre-State relations. The Finance Commission, All India Services and President’s Rule are subjects associated with constitutional provisions, not the two commissions asked about here.

s: Which constitutional provision assigns residuary powers to the Union in the context of Indian federalism?
x: Article 248 deals with residuary powers with the Union. Article 263 concerns the Inter-State Council, Article 280 the Finance Commission, and Article 356 President’s Rule.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Indian federalism?
o: S.R. Bommai (1994) held federalism to be part of the Basic Structure and curbed Article 356
Article 1(1) describes India, that is Bharat, as a 'Union of States'
In State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to Governor (2023), the SC held that Governors may indefinitely delay assent to Bills
State of West Bengal v. Union of India (1962) described India as quasi-federal
x: The 2023 Punjab case held that Governors cannot indefinitely delay assent to Bills; the other three statements are correct.

s: Which case laid down the requirement of quantifiable data for conditions relating to promotion quota?
x: M. Nagaraj laid down the quantifiable-data requirement; Indra Sawhney prescribed the creamy layer for OBCs.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Inter-State Council?
x: Article 263 deals with the Inter-State Council; Article 280 is the Finance Commission, 356 President's Rule and 312 All India Services.

s: What term has been used to describe a Governor's delay in giving assent to Bills?
x: Gubernatorial delays in assent have been described as a pocket veto.

s: For which region was Sixth Schedule status demanded in the debate on Indian federalism?
x: Sixth Schedule status was sought for Ladakh, while Bihar and Odisha sought Special Category Status.

s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for Special Category Status under the Gadgil-Mukherjee framework?
o: High population density in urban areas
Low population density or a sizeable tribal population
x: The criterion is low population density or a sizeable tribal population, not high urban population density.

s: In which year was the domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha membership removed?
x: The domicile requirement was removed in 2003; vertical devolution is formally 41%.

s: Of the 16th Finance Commission grants to Telangana's rural local bodies, what share goes to Gram Panchayats?
x: GPs get 80%, intermediate and district panchayats 10% each, of Telangana's ₹9,968 crore.

s: What share of the divisible pool goes to the States as vertical devolution under the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Vertical devolution is formally 41%; cesses and surcharges lie outside the divisible pool.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court apply the creamy layer exclusion to OBC reservation?
x: Indra Sawhney (1992) introduced the creamy layer for OBCs; M. Nagaraj asked for quantifiable data on promotion quota.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the All India Services?
x: Article 312 provides for the All India Services.

o: Ministry of Panchayati Raj and Ministry of Rural Development jointly

o: India’s first comprehensive data-driven framework to assess Gram Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies
India’s first framework to assess State Finance Commissions
India’s first framework to rank National Panchayati Raj institutions
India’s first framework to assess only urban local bodies

s: Which State did not participate in the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) 2.0?

s: What is the main cause of death in stampedes?

s: Which of the following is NOT a measure recommended in NDMA guidelines for preventing stampedes?
o: Real-time monitoring through CCTV and drones
Capacity mapping to keep crowds within safe limits
x: The NDMA recommends public address systems, so eliminating them is not a recommended measure.

s:
Arrange the following countries in chronological order of the grant of universal adult franchise:
1. India
2. Japan
3. Sri Lanka
4. United States of America
x: The correct order is United States of America in 1920, Sri Lanka in 1931, Japan in 1945 and India in 1950. Therefore, the sequence is 4-3-2-1.

s: As per NCRB Crime in India 2023, how many of the 180 cases of denial of access to public spaces to SCs were from Uttar Pradesh?
x: Uttar Pradesh accounted for 173 of the 180 cases in 2023.

s: Which country was the first to give women the right to vote, in 1893?
x: New Zealand was the first country to give women the vote, in 1893, associated with Kate Sheppard. The United States, Sri Lanka and Japan correspond to later stages in the stated sequence of universal adult franchise.

s: Which Directive Principle Article concerns the organisation of village panchayats?
x: Article 40 concerns organising village panchayats; Part IX and the 11th Schedule came from the 73rd Amendment.

s: Article 17, which abolishes untouchability, is part of which Fundamental Right?
x: Article 17 is part of the Right to Equality (Articles 14–18), not the Right to Freedom.

s:
Assertion (A): Section 4 of the SC/ST Act penalises officials’ neglect.
Reason (R): The Protection of Civil Rights Act was enacted in 1989.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Assertion A is true because Section 4 of the SC/ST Act penalises officials’ neglect. Reason R is false: the Protection of Civil Rights Act was enacted in 1955, while 1989 is associated with the SC/ST Act.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding women's representation in the Lok Sabha is incorrect?
o: Women MPs numbered 78 in 2019, the highest among the listed years.
x: The incorrect statement is that women MPs numbered 74 in 2014; the correct figure for 2014 was 62. The figure of 74 applied to 2024, while 2019 recorded the highest figure among these years at 78.

s: Who conducted the Women and Politics Survey (2019)?
x: The Lokniti-CSDS Women and Politics Survey (2019) found many women needed family permission to take part.

s: Which State topped the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) 2.0?
x: Tripura was the top State, with about 80% of its Panchayats as Front Runners; UP had the highest participation.

s: In which category did the largest number of Gram Panchayats fall under PAI 2.0?
x: Performer (B) was the largest group with 1,18,824 Panchayats (about 45.72%); no GP reached A+.

s: Which district has the highest cancer incidence in the Cancer Atlas of Telangana 2026?
x: Hanumakonda has the highest incidence (79 per lakh), followed by Hyderabad (72).

s: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule for Panchayats?
x: The 73rd Amendment (1992) added the 11th Schedule with 29 subjects for Panchayats.

s: Which State recorded the highest participation in the Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0, with all its 57,678 Gram Panchayats?
x: Uttar Pradesh had all 57,678 GPs assessed; Tripura was the top State in performance.

s: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment provided what under Articles 15(6) and 16(6)?
o: Reservation for SEBCs, SCs and STs
x: The 103rd Amendment of 2019 provided 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections under Articles 15(6) and 16(6). Reservation in promotion for SC/ST is associated with Article 16(4A), not these provisions.

s: Against whom, and by whom, does Article 15(1) prohibit discrimination?
x: Article 15(1) bars the State from discriminating against citizens; descent is not one of its listed grounds.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the BCCI?
o: It is substantially controlled and financed by the government.
It is a private society under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, 1975.
Zee Telefilms v. Union of India (2005) held it not to be 'State' under Article 12.
The CIC held in May 2026 that it is not a public authority under the RTI Act.
x: The BCCI is a private society not substantially controlled or financed by the government.

s: In its ruling of 18 May 2026, how did the Central Information Commission classify the BCCI under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act, 2005?
o: It is a public authority only for cricket administration
It is a public authority in every respect
It is a security body exempt under Section 24
It is not a public authority
x: The Central Information Commission held on 18 May 2026 that the BCCI is not a public authority under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act, 2005. The ruling did not classify the BCCI as a security body or as a public authority for cricket administration.

s: According to the Supreme Court ruling concerning the inclusion of Rajasthani in a teacher recruitment examination syllabus, what was recognised as part of the right to identity?
o: Thinking and expressing in one’s own language
Only instruction in a mother tongue at the primary stage
Only the preference for mother tongue under NEP 2020
Inclusion of every regional language in every teacher recruitment examination
x: The Supreme Court recognised that thinking and expressing in one’s language forms part of the right to identity. Article 350A concerns instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for linguistic minority children, while NEP 2020 favours mother tongue; neither creates the broader claim in the other options.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the earlier CIC ruling on the BCCI is incorrect?
o: In 2018, the CIC held the BCCI to be a public authority.
The 2018 decision was given by Information Commissioner M. Sridhar Acharyulu.
The 2018 CIC holding declared that the BCCI was not a public authority.
The Madras High Court set aside the 2018 CIC holding.
x: The incorrect statement is that the 2018 CIC holding declared the BCCI not to be a public authority. The holding instead treated the BCCI as a public authority, and it was subsequently set aside by the Madras High Court.

s: What did the Law Commission’s 275th Report of 2018 recommend in relation to the BCCI?
o: Limiting RTI coverage to the BCCI’s e-sports activities
Exempting the BCCI from Article 226 review
Treating the BCCI as a security body under the Second Schedule
Bringing the BCCI under the RTI framework
x: The Law Commission’s 275th Report, issued in 2018, recommended that the BCCI be brought under the RTI framework. The other options do not state the recommendation associated with that report.

s: To what extent are government-funded sports bodies covered by RTI under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025?
o: Only to the extent of the government funds
Only in matters of corruption and human rights
x: Government-funded sports bodies are subject to RTI only to the extent of those funds; the corruption/human-rights exception applies to exempt security bodies.

s: Under the UGC Promotion of Equity in HEIs Regulations, 2026, which body functions as the nodal body in every institution?
x: The Regulations provide for an Equal Opportunity Centre as the nodal body in every higher educational institution.

s: Amid which concerns did the Supreme Court's interim stay on the UGC Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions Regulations, 2026 come?
x: The context was caste discrimination and student suicides, including the Abeda Salim Tadvi case.

s: What kind of grievance system do the UGC Equity Regulations, 2026 provide for?
o: Only an online portal during working hours
A 24/7 system with helplines, portals, Equity Officers and Equity Squads
Complaints only through the State Government
x: The Regulations provide a 24/7 grievance system with helplines, portals, Equity Officers and Equity Squads.

s: Which clause of Article 15 enables special provisions for women and children?
x: Article 15(3) concerns special provisions for women and children; 15(4) covers SEBCs, SCs and STs and 15(5) educational institutions.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for children of linguistic minorities?
x: Article 350A asks States to provide mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage to linguistic-minority children.

s: The Lodha Committee is associated with reforms in which body?
x: In BCCI v. Cricket Association of Bihar (2016) the Supreme Court backed the Lodha Committee reforms of the BCCI.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 16(4A) for reservation in promotion for SCs and STs?
x: The 77th Amendment (1995) inserted Article 16(4A); the 103rd (2019) gave 10% EWS reservation.

s: Under Section 24 of the RTI Act, information from exempted security organisations can still be sought on which matters?
x: Security bodies in the Second Schedule are exempt, except for information on corruption and human rights violations.

s: Which body functions under the Agriculture Ministry and classifies pesticides into four toxicity classes based on LD50?
x: CIBRC functions under the Agriculture Ministry and classifies pesticides into four toxicity classes by LD50. FSSAI sets MRLs, while the Central Pesticides Board and Registration Committee have separate roles under the pesticides framework.

s: With reference to the Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025, identify the incorrect statement.
o: It replaces the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971.
It is administered under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.
It provides for a Central Pesticides Board and a Registration Committee.
It includes bio-pesticides within its coverage.
x: The incorrect statement is that the Bill is administered under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers. It is under the Ministry of Agriculture; the Bill replaces the specified insecticides law and rules, covers bio-pesticides, and provides for the Central Pesticides Board and Registration Committee.

s: Why was discussion on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 deferred by the Union government?
o: A Supreme Court order relating to foreign contributions
Opposition concerns over minority-led institutions and civil society
The expiry of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
A disagreement over the Consolidated Fund of India
x: Discussion on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 was deferred after opposition concerns over minority-led institutions and civil society. The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 is the parent Act, not the reason stated for the deferment.

s: What is the Designated Authority meant to do under the FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026?
o: Take over and manage foreign contributions and assets of bodies whose registration is cancelled, surrendered or expired
Approve foreign contributions before they are received
Audit annual returns of FCRA-registered bodies
x: The Designated Authority takes over and manages the foreign contributions and assets of bodies whose registration has ceased.

s: What does the FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026 do to restrictions on persons in news production and broadcasting?
x: The Bill expands, not removes, restrictions on persons in news production and broadcasting.

s: Which body sets the Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) for pesticides in India?
o: Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee
x: MRLs are set by FSSAI, not the Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee.

s: The Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 is under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: The Bill, replacing the Insecticides Act, 1968, is under the Agriculture Ministry, not Chemicals and Fertilizers.

s: Which Act will the Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 replace?
x: The draft Bill replaces the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971.

s: What did the NSE launch as a dedicated segment in May 2026?
x: NSE launched a dedicated segment for Electronic Gold Receipts, which are SEBI-regulated securities backed by physical gold in approved vaults. Unclaimed deposits, AIFs and maritime insurance are separate financial-sector developments.

s: Under SEBI’s GARUDA mechanism, the approval timeline for schemes of non-accredited investors is reduced from 30 to what number of working days?
x: GARUDA reduces the timeline for non-accredited investor schemes from 30 to 10 working days. The other periods are not specified as the revised GARUDA timeline.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Category III AIFs are hedge funds; Category I covers startups and Category II private equity, and SEBI (set up 1988) got statutory status in 1992.

s: Which organisation has been designated as the PaRRVA Agency for verifying past risk and return claims?
x: CARE Ratings is the PaRRVA Agency, while NSE serves as the PaRRVA Data Centre. PaRRVA verifies performance claims of advisers, research analysts and algo providers.

s: Which entities collaborated to detect and freeze mule accounts through an MoU-related initiative?
x: I4C and the RBI Innovation Hub collaborated to detect and freeze mule accounts. The RBI Innovation Hub was established in Bengaluru in 2022, while I4C was established in 2018 under the MHA; EPFO and MoSPI are not the partners identified for this initiative.

s: Why was SEBI's Cyber-suraksha.ai Task Force (May 2026) set up?
x: The task force deals with AI-driven cyber threats; Sudarshan tracks finfluencers, PaRRVA verifies claims and GARUDA speeds AIF approvals.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about recent SEBI tools and mechanisms?
o: GARUDA cuts approval for non-accredited investor schemes from 30 to 10 working days.
CARE Ratings is the PaRRVA Agency.
Sudarshan is SEBI's in-house AI to monitor finfluencers.
x: NSE is the PaRRVA Data Centre; CARE Ratings is the PaRRVA Agency.

s: Who is the Chairperson of SEBI?
x: Tuhin Kanta Pandey heads SEBI, set up on 12 April 1988 and made statutory on 30 January 1992.

s: In which year did SEBI get statutory status?
x: SEBI was set up on 12 April 1988 and became statutory on 30 January 1992.

s: Procurement of 20 lakh MT of potatoes under the Market Intervention Scheme was approved under which umbrella scheme?
x: The potato procurement was approved under PM-AASHA on a State's request.

s: How much did the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme receive in Budget 2026–27?
x: ECMS was allotted ₹40,000 crore in Budget 2026–27; NITI Aayog has partnered Tata Electronics on electronics manufacturing.

s: What does VAANI, the AICTE initiative for technical education in Indian languages, stand for?
o: Vocational Advancement and Accreditation Network for Indian Education
Virtual Access for Academic Networks and New India
Vibrant Advocacy for Advancement and Nurturing of Indian Languages
Vision for Applied Analytics and New Innovation
x: VAANI stands for Vibrant Advocacy for Advancement and Nurturing of Indian Languages. The initiative focuses on advancing technical education through Indian languages.

s: From which date did sale of E20 petrol become mandatory at all petrol pumps across India?
x: E20 sale became mandatory at all petrol pumps from 1 April 2026; the EBP programme began in 2003.

s: The NITI Aayog–UNICEF India partnership on nutrition in aspirational districts is associated with which platform?
x: The partnership addresses nutrition and health in aspirational districts and blocks through the IMPAct4Nutrition platform.

s: Up to when did the CCEA extend the SARTHAK-PDS Central Scheme?
x: SARTHAK-PDS was extended to March 2031 with an outlay of ₹25,530 crore.

s: The Ministry of Culture signed an agreement with FICCI for which purpose?
o: Preparing a national electronics manufacturing strategy
Preparing a national nutrition and health strategy
Preparing a national cultural and creative economy strategy
x: The Ministry of Culture–FICCI agreement concerns a national cultural and creative economy strategy. Electronics manufacturing, nutrition and health, and pension services relate to other initiatives.

s: Which CBI initiative helps citizens verify CBI notices and curb digital arrest frauds?
x: Abhay is the CBI's AI chatbot for verifying CBI notices and curbing digital arrest frauds.

s: Which of the following about recent digital governance and market tools is NOT correct?
o: PRARAMBH, for the Income Tax Act 2025, includes the 'Kar Saathi' AI chatbot.
SEBI's 'Sudarshan' is an in-house AI tool for monitoring finfluencers.
The 'Jeni Keyboard' of Hyped Samvadini translates in 2009+ languages.
UIDAI's bug bounty programme concerns Aadhaar security.
x: Jeni Keyboard supports translation in 55+ languages, not 2009+; the other statements are correct.

s: Which authority runs the 1855 toll-free helpline for Census 2027?
x: The 1855 helpline and WhatsApp chatbot for Census 2027 are run by the Registrar General of India.

s: Which body launched 'Arogya One' for planting medicinal plants along highways?
x: Arogya One is an NHAI initiative; phase 1 covers 17 locations, including in Andhra Pradesh.

s: The PRARAMBH income-tax awareness campaign from 1 April 2026 is for which new law that replaces the Act of 1961?
x: PRARAMBH spreads awareness of the Income Tax Act 2025, which replaces the 1961 Act; CBDT runs it with the 'Kar Saathi' chatbot.

s: Under which Act does the CBI work?
x: The CBI (1963) draws its legal powers from the DSPE Act, 1946.

s: Under which policy was the E20 petrol target set?
x: The E20 target (2025-26) comes from the National Policy on Biofuels 2018, amended in 2022; the Ethanol Blended Petrol programme began in 2003.

s: Which combination was identified as a driver of the renewed concern over zoonotic spillovers during the Hantavirus outbreak?
o: Deforestation, climate change, telemedicine and global travel
Deforestation, climate change, industrial livestock farming and global travel
Industrial livestock farming, geo-tagging, climate change and global travel
Deforestation, unpasteurised milk, industrial livestock farming and global travel
x: The identified drivers were deforestation, climate change, industrial livestock farming and global travel. Telemedicine, geo-tagging and unpasteurised milk are not included in this list of drivers.

s: Where was SJVN, which is building the Lower Arun hydropower project in Nepal, established in 1988?
x: SJVN dates to 1988 at Shimla; Lower Arun is its second Nepal project after Arun-3.

s: What is the vector of the paddy dwarfing disease reported in Punjab?
x: The disease, caused by SRBSDV, is spread by the white-backed plant hopper and was first reported in Punjab in 2022.

s: India's first women SHG-managed solar plant (1 MW) at Venkatapuram is in which district of Telangana?
x: The 1 MW plant is at Venkatapuram in Khammam, linked to the Indira Mahila Shakti Scheme.

s: Which State ranked first under the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm?
x: Telangana ranked first under NMEO-Oil Palm, which was launched in 2021.

s: Which of the following statements about the Kakatiya Mega Textile Park is incorrect?
o: It is the country's first PM MITRA Park at Warangal.
An investment of ₹6,000 crore is expected.
It is expected to generate 24,400 jobs.

s: The renewed Hantavirus outbreak highlighted zoonotic spillover through exposure to which materials from infected rodents?
o: Water or soil containing animal urine
x: Hantavirus spreads through the urine, droppings and saliva of infected rodents. Fleas on rodents are associated with plague, while water or soil with animal urine is linked to leptospirosis.

s: How does plague mainly spread to humans?
x: Plague spreads through fleas on rodents; Nipah via bats, pigs and fruit; brucellosis via cattle and milk; rabies via dogs and bats.

s: What is the capacity of SJVN's Lower Arun run-of-river project in Nepal?
x: Lower Arun is 679 MW; SJVN's earlier Nepal project Arun-3 is 900 MW.

s: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
x: The Koshi is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'; the Arun river of Nepal is its tributary.

s: Which is the country's first PM MITRA Park?
x: The Kakatiya Mega Textile Park at Warangal (1,327 acres) is the country's first PM MITRA Park.

s: What weight does income distance carry in the 16th Finance Commission's horizontal devolution criteria?
x: Income distance has 42.5%, 2011 population 17.5% and demographic performance 10%.

s: Which of the following was NOT a horizontal devolution criterion of the 15th Finance Commission?
x: Contribution to GDP is the new criterion added by the 16th FC; the 15th FC used demographic performance, forest and ecology, and tax and fiscal effort.

s: Who chaired the 16th Finance Commission, whose report covered the award period 2026–2031?
x: Arvind Panagariya chaired the 16th Finance Commission, whose award period was 2026–2031. N.K. Singh chaired the 15th Finance Commission, while Y.V. Reddy and Vijay Kelkar chaired the 14th and 13th Finance Commissions respectively.

s: Which horizontal devolution criterion was removed by the 16th Finance Commission when 'contribution to GDP' was newly added?
x: The tax and fiscal effort criterion was removed and contribution to GDP was added.

s: The 16th Finance Commission retained the States' share at 41%; what share had the States demanded?
x: States demanded 50%, but the 16th FC retained the 41% share.

s: In what ratio are local body grants split between basic and performance grants under the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Local body grants have an 80% basic and 20% performance structure; 90:10 is the disaster-cost sharing for NE and Himalayan states.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 16th Finance Commission's fiscal recommendations?
o: States should cap their fiscal deficit at 3% of GSDP
The Centre's fiscal deficit should be 4% of GDP by 2030–31
x: The Centre's target is 3.5% of GDP by 2030–31, not 4%.

s: At what level did the 16th Finance Commission (award period 2026-31) keep vertical devolution to States?
x: Vertical devolution was kept at 41%; a new contribution-to-GDP criterion with 10% weight was added.

s: On which date was the report of the 16th Finance Commission tabled in the Lok Sabha?
x: The 16th Finance Commission report was tabled in the Lok Sabha on 1 February 2026.

s: Which grants were dropped in the 16th Finance Commission award, drawing criticism that it placed efficiency above equity?
x: Revenue-deficit grants were dropped and the income-distance weight was reduced.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Inter-State Council?
x: Article 263 provides for the Inter-State Council; Article 280 is the Finance Commission.

s: On which date was the 16th Finance Commission constituted?
x: It was constituted on 31 December 2023; members were notified on 30 January 2024.

s: Population growth during which period is the basis of the 16th Finance Commission's demographic performance criterion?
x: Demographic performance uses population growth 1971–2011, not TFR.

s: Which change did the 16th Finance Commission make to the forest and ecology criterion?
x: The forest criterion kept its 10% weight but now includes open forests.

s: What is the disaster cost-sharing ratio between the Centre and North-Eastern and Himalayan States under the 16th Finance Commission?
x: NE and Himalayan States share 90:10; other States 75:25.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 16th Finance Commission award?
o: The government accepted the 41% vertical share
Tax and fiscal effort was retained as a criterion
Local body grants are split 80:20 basic to performance
x: Tax and fiscal effort was removed by the 16th FC.

s: Why did the divisible pool's share of gross tax revenue fall from 89.1% in 2014-15?
x: Cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool, so their rise shrank it to about 74–80%.

s: Which Finance Commission raised the States' share of the divisible pool from 32% to 42%?
x: The 14th Finance Commission under Y.V. Reddy raised the States' share from 32% to 42%.

s: Who was the chairman of the First Finance Commission?
x: The 1st Finance Commission (1951) was chaired by K.C. Neogy.

x: Population's weight was raised to 17.5%; income distance has 42.5%.

x: The Tamil Nadu (DMK) government set up the Rajamannar Committee in 1969 to study Centre-State relations.

s: Which body did the Rajamannar Committee want set up at once under Article 263?
x: The Rajamannar Committee called for the immediate setting up of the Inter-State Council under Article 263.

s: In which year was the Inter-State Council set up under Article 263?
x: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990, following the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation.

s: Who was the chairman of the 14th Finance Commission?
x: The 14th Finance Commission (2013) was chaired by Y.V. Reddy; it raised the States' share from 32% to 42%.

s: Who chaired the committee on Centre-State relations set up by the Tamil Nadu Government in 1969?
x: Dr P.V. Rajamannar, a former Chief Justice of the Madras High Court, chaired this State-level committee.

s: In India's counter-terrorism policy PRAHAAR, CBRNED stands for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, Explosive and what?
x: PRAHAAR defines CBRNED as Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, Explosive and Digital.

s: On which date did the Ministry of Home Affairs release PRAHAAR, India's first national counter-terrorism policy?
x: PRAHAAR was released on 23 February 2026 and has seven pillars, including Prevention and Recovery and resilience.

s: Under PRAHAAR, India’s national counter-terrorism policy, what does the zero-tolerance approach seek to deny terrorists?
o: Crypto funding, dark web access and cyber-attacks by nation-states
x: PRAHAAR’s zero-tolerance approach seeks to deny terrorists funds, weapons and safe havens. Power, railways and aviation are critical sectors, while the other options refer to separate threat categories or manifestations identified in the policy.

s: What position does PRAHAAR adopt regarding the relationship between terrorism and social or civilisational identities?
o: It links terrorism to civilisation but not to religion or ethnicity.
It links terrorism exclusively to one religion.
It links terrorism to ethnicity but not to religion or civilisation.
It does not link terrorism to any religion, ethnicity or civilisation.
x: PRAHAAR does not link terrorism to any religion, ethnicity or civilisation. The other options introduce identity-based linkages that the policy explicitly avoids.

s: NATGRID has been integrated with which database for population-scale surveillance?
x: NATGRID was expanded into population-scale surveillance and integrated with the NPR.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NATGRID?
o: It handles tens of thousands of queries a month, including from state police
Its analytical tools include entity resolution, facial recognition and machine learning
It originated as a response to the 2001 Parliament attack
It engages the right to privacy recognised in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017)
x: NATGRID originated as a response to the 26/11 Mumbai attacks in 2008.

s: What was the distinguishing national-level feature of NIDMS, launched by the Ministry of Home Affairs in January 2026?
o: India's first national IED data platform
India's first digital creators' content platform
x: NIDMS was India's first national IED data platform and was built by the National Bomb Data Centre of the NSG. The other options describe land data, digital creators' content or legal services rather than IED data.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PRAHAAR?
o: It recognises cyber-attacks by nation-states as a threat
It recognises crypto funding as a terrorism-related threat
It treats cyber-attacks as terrorism only when carried out by non-state actors
It recognises the dark web as a terrorism-related threat
x: PRAHAAR specifically recognises cyber-attacks by nation-states, so limiting it to non-state actors is wrong.

s: How many pillars does PRAHAAR, India's national counter-terrorism policy, have?
x: PRAHAAR rests on seven pillars, from Prevention to Recovery and resilience.

s: Which body built NIDMS, India's first national IED data platform?
o: National Bomb Data Centre of the NSG
Ministry of Home Affairs' LWE Division
x: NIDMS was built by the National Bomb Data Centre (NSG) and launched at Manesar.

s: NATGRID was conceived as a response to which event?
x: NATGRID originated after 26/11 to integrate fragmented intelligence databases.

s: On what basis are funds allocated under the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority?
x: FNTA funds are based on population and area; the Mini-Secretariat is headed by a senior officer.

s: The Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority has powers over how many subjects?
x: The Authority has powers over 46 subjects, including land use, agriculture, rural development and infrastructure.

s: Which Article, concerning Nagaland's customary law, remains intact under the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority agreement?
x: Article 371(A) remains intact; the Authority covers Kiphire, Longleng, Mon, Noklak, Shamator and Tuensang.

s: The tripartite agreement creating the institutional framework for eastern Nagaland was signed on 5 February 2026 among which parties?
o: The Centre, the Rajya Sabha and the Nagaland Government
The Centre, the Manipur Government and the Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation
The Nagaland Government, the Hill Areas Committee and the Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation
The Centre, the Nagaland Government and the Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation
x: The agreement was tripartite among the Centre, the Nagaland Government and the Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation. The Hill Areas Committee is associated with a similar model in Manipur, not with the three-party agreement.

s: Which district is NOT part of the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority?
x: FNTA covers Kiphire, Longleng, Mon, Noklak, Shamator and Tuensang; Dimapur is excluded.

s: Under which Article does the Hill Areas Committee of Manipur, a model similar to FNTA, function?
x: The Hill Areas Committee is under Article 371(C); 371(A) concerns Nagaland.

s: In which year did Nagaland become a State?
x: Nagaland became a State in 1963; ENPO later demanded a separate Frontier Nagaland State.

s: Which hill range separates Manipur and Nagaland?
x: The Barail range separates Manipur and Nagaland.

o: They involve voluntary contributions and are not financed from the Consolidated Fund of India.

s: In 2020, to which fund did the Supreme Court refuse to transfer PM CARES money?
x: The SC refused the transfer of PM CARES money to the NDRF; CAG audit applies to the NDRF, not PM CARES.

s: Which Parliamentary Friendship Group is correctly matched with its chair?
x: Shashi Tharoor chairs the France group. USA is chaired by Baijayant Panda, Israel by Ravi Shankar Prasad and Japan by Manish Tewari.

s: Each Parliamentary Friendship Group formed by Speaker Om Birla has how many members?
x: Groups were formed with 64 countries, each having 11 members.

s: Who chairs the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025?

s: What does the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, referred to a JPC, concern?
o: Removal of PM, CMs and Ministers held in custody
