s: The UGC Promotion of Equity in HEIs Regulations, 2026, covering SCs, STs and OBCs, align with which Articles?
x: The regulations align with Articles 15(4) and 15(5); OBCs were excluded only in the draft.

s: In which year was the University Education Commission headed by Dr. S. Radhakrishnan set up?
x: The University Education Commission dates to 1948, after the Sargeant Report (1944) and the committee for Aligarh, Banaras and Delhi universities (1945).

s: The Election Commission of India is established under which Article and from which year?
x: The Election Commission of India is established under Article 324 and dates from 1950. The alternatives alter either the constitutional Article or the year of establishment.

s: The UGC Promotion of Equity in HEIs Regulations, 2026, notified to address caste-based discrimination, replaced which earlier regulations?
x: The 2026 regulations replaced the 2012 regulations. The other years are incorrect because the earlier regulations replaced by the new framework were from 2012.

s: How often must the Equity Committee meet at least under the UGC Equity Regulations, 2026?
x: The Equity Committee must meet at least twice a year, not once.

s: Which provision of the draft was dropped from the final UGC Equity Regulations, 2026?
o: Equal Opportunity Centre in every HEI
Annual equity compliance report to the UGC
Equity Committee chaired by the Head of Institution
Fine on students for false complaints
x: The fine for false complaints (and the OBC exclusion) was dropped; the other provisions remain.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The NCW is a statutory body set up in 1992 under the NCW Act, 1990
The NCST is a constitutional body under Article 338A
The NCST was established on 19 February 2004
The previous ECI National Conference of State Election Commissions was held in 2000
x: The previous ECI conference was held in 1999, not 2000.

s: Who inaugurated the UGC in 1953?
x: The UGC, established in 1952, was inaugurated by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad in 1953 and became statutory under the UGC Act, 1956.

s: From which Article does the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes derive its constitutional status?
x: NCST is provided under Article 338A. Article 338 relates to NCSC, Article 338B to NCBC and Article 280 to the Finance Commission.

s: Which of the following bodies is statutory rather than constitutional?
x: NCW was set up under the NCW Act, 1990; the others are constitutional.

s: What is the nature of the Law Commission of India?
o: Non-statutory body set up by government notification
Statutory body under an Act of 1990
x: The Law Commission is executive (non-statutory), set up by notification with terms of reference.

s: Who chairs the 23rd Law Commission of India?
x: Justice Dinesh Maheshwari chairs it; Hitesh Jain and D.P. Verma are full-time members.

s: Who is the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women?
x: Vijaya Rahatkar chairs the NCW; Antar Singh Arya chairs the NCST.

s: The ECI's National Conference of State Election Commissions in February 2026 was the first since which year?
x: It was the first such conference in about 27 years, the last being in 1999.

s: What did the Sargeant Report of 1944 recommend setting up?
x: The 1944 Sargeant Report recommended a University Grants Committee.

s: In which year did the UGC, established in 1952, become a statutory body?
x: The UGC became statutory under the UGC Act, 1956.

s: Who is the chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
x: Antar Singh Arya chairs the NCST, a constitutional body under Article 338A.

s: What is the term of the 23rd Law Commission of India?
x: The 23rd Law Commission has a three-year term from 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2027.

s: What is the motto of the University Grants Commission?
x: The UGC motto, 'Gyan-Vigyan Vimuktaye', means 'Knowledge Liberates' and appears in its logo.

s: Who was the Chief Election Commissioner at the ECI's National Conference of State Election Commissions in February 2026?
x: CEC Gyanesh Kumar held the conference on 24 February 2026 with ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

s: The Thorat Committee (2007) is associated with which issue?
x: The Thorat Committee (2007) looked into caste discrimination against SC/ST students and is cited for the UGC equity rules.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ad hoc judges in High Courts?
o: Ad hoc judges are appointed under Article 224A
Articles 214–231 deal with the Supreme Court
Their number is capped at 10% of the sanctioned strength
Retired High Court judges may serve as ad hoc judges
x: Articles 214–231 concern the High Courts, not the Supreme Court.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court recognise the Public Trust Doctrine, which originated in Roman law?
o: M.C. Mehta vs Union of India (1987)
x: The Supreme Court recognised the Public Trust Doctrine in M.C. Mehta vs Kamal Nath (1997).

s: Justice Lisa Gill was recommended as Chief Justice of which High Court?
x: The SC collegium recommended Justice Lisa Gill for the AP High Court and Justice Suresh Aravind for Madras.

s: How many of the 25 High Courts appointed ad hoc judges after the Supreme Court permitted them under Article 224A?
x: None of the 25 High Courts acted on the permission.

s: Which provision provides for disqualification for promoting enmity?
o: Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
x: RPA Section 8 covers disqualification for promoting enmity; BNS 353 covers incitement endangering public order.

s: What did the Bezbaruah Committee of 2014 deal with?
x: The Bezbaruah Committee dealt with racial and regional discrimination; mob lynching guidelines came from Tehseen Poonawalla (2018).

s: What was the key distinction of the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025?
o: Karnataka became the first State to bring a dedicated law on untouchability
Karnataka became the first State to bring a dedicated law only on hate speech
Karnataka became the first State to bring a dedicated law only on hate crimes
Karnataka became the first State to bring a dedicated law on hate speech and hate crimes
x: Karnataka was the first State to bring a dedicated law on hate speech and hate crimes. The tempting alternatives narrow its scope to only hate speech or only hate crimes, whereas the Bill covers both.

s: In which case was Section 66A of the IT Act struck down?
x: Section 66A was struck down in Shreya Singhal (2015).

s: What major legal gap was highlighted in connection with the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025?
o: India has no provision for disqualification for promoting enmity
India has no provision dealing with untouchability
India has no law on mob lynching guidelines
India has no statutory definition of hate speech
x: The highlighted gap was that India has no statutory definition of hate speech. The other options refer to subjects dealt with under other legal provisions or judicial guidelines, not the specific gap identified.

s: Under the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025, on whom does collective liability for hate speech linked to an organisation fall?
o: Only the person making the speech
Only the publisher of the content
x: The Bill provides for collective liability of office-bearers of linked organisations.

s: What does the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025 empower the State to do about online hateful content?
o: Only refer such content to the Centre
Only seek court orders for removal
x: The Bill empowers the State to block or remove hateful online content.

s: Which new Sections did Law Commission Report 267 (2017) on hate speech propose?
x: Law Commission Report 267 (2017) proposed new Sections 153C and 505A.

s: In Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan (2014), what did the Supreme Court ask the Law Commission to do?
x: The SC asked the Law Commission to define hate speech; mob lynching guidelines came in Tehseen Poonawalla.

s: What did the Viswanathan Committee (2015) deal with?
x: The Viswanathan Committee dealt with identity-based offences; Bezbaruah with racial discrimination.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court issue guidelines against mob lynching?
x: Tehseen Poonawalla (2018) laid down guidelines on mob lynching.

s: Which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaces IPC Section 153A on promoting enmity between groups?
x: BNS Section 196 is the former IPC 153A; Section 299 is the former 295A.

s: Census 2027 is to include caste enumeration for the first time since which Census?
x: Caste enumeration returns for the first time since 1931; the Census is conducted by the RGCC under the MHA.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a commission on backward classes?
x: Article 340 provides for a commission on backward classes.

s: In which year was the Criminal Tribes Act, which labelled tribes as 'born criminals', enacted?
x: The Criminal Tribes Act dates from 1871; 1872 and 1881 are census years.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 8th Economic Census proposed for 2027?
o: It will help build a Statistical Business Register
It covers establishments meant solely for personal consumption
The NSO conducts it with State Directorates of Economics & Statistics
x: The Economic Census covers establishments producing or distributing goods and services, except those meant solely for personal consumption.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2026–27 Population Census?
o: It will be the first fully digital Census with self-enumeration.
It will be the 15th decennial Census.
It will have a separate head for transgender-headed households.
Its first phase (House Listing) runs from 1 April to 30 September 2026.
x: It will be the 16th decennial Census, not the 15th.

s: Which sequence correctly describes the planned Population Census and 8th Economic Census?
o: 8th Economic Census in 2026 followed by Population Census in 2027
Population Census in 2026–27 followed by the 8th Economic Census in 2027
Population Census in 2027 followed by the 8th Economic Census in 2026–27
Both censuses will be conducted simultaneously in 2026–27
x: The two-phase Population Census is scheduled for 2026–27, followed by the 8th Economic Census in 2027. The other options reverse or incorrectly merge the sequence.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about census and backward-class provisions?
o: The Registrar General & Census Commissioner functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs
Census is placed in Entry 69 of the Concurrent List
The Census Act, 1948 keeps individual census data confidential
Article 340 provides for a commission on backward classes
x: Census is in Entry 69 of the Union List, not the Concurrent List.

s: Which of the following census year – milestone pairs is correctly matched?
o: 1921 – First complete census of a city
x: 1881 saw the first synchronous census. 1830 was the first complete city census, 1872 the first all-India non-synchronous census and 1921 the Great Divide.

s: Who conducts the Census of India?
o: Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under MHA
x: The RGI under the Ministry of Home Affairs conducts the Census.

s: Under whom was India's first synchronous census of 1881 conducted?
x: 1881 was the first synchronous census under Plowden; 1872 (Mayo) was non-synchronous.

s: What is the name of the unified enterprise database that the 8th Economic Census aims to build?
x: The 8th Economic Census will build a Statistical Business Register.

s: In which year was the first Economic Census held in India?
x: The first Economic Census was held in 1977; the 8th is due in 2027.

s: Under which Viceroy was the first all-India, non-synchronous Census held in 1872?
x: The 1872 Census was held under Lord Mayo; the first synchronous Census was in 1881.

s: Under which Act is the Census of India conducted?
o: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
x: The Census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948, which keeps individual data confidential.

s: Which Census year is known as the 'Great Divide' because India's population declined that decade?
x: The 1921 Census showed the only decadal decline (-0.31%), linked to the 1918 influenza.

s: Who conducted the first complete census of a city, Dacca, in 1830?
x: Henry Walter carried out the 1830 census of Dacca, the first complete census of a city.

s: Which High Court upheld the Bihar caste survey in 2023?
x: The Patna High Court upheld the Bihar caste survey in 2023; the Supreme Court issued notice.

s: Which distinction is associated with the Salal Hydroelectric Project in the context of the Indus Waters Treaty framework?
o: It was the first rural road project in Mandi district
It was the first vertical-lift sea railway bridge in India
It was India’s first coal-to-SNG project
It was the first hydropower project built by India in Kashmir under the IWT framework
x: Salal was the first hydropower project built by India in Kashmir under the Indus Waters Treaty framework. The vertical-lift bridge, coal-to-SNG project and rural road are separate developments.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the airport monetisation model and sector outlook?
o: The model shifted from revenue-sharing to a per-passenger fee, with tariffs regulated by AERA
AERA may impose tariff cuts up to 10% for missing service benchmarks
Only 6% of Indians fly, and 50 new airports are planned in five years
The airport network is expected to reach 163 airports
x: AERA penalties can include tariff cuts of up to 5%, not 10%.

s: According to the NITI Aayog report on end-of-life vehicles, what was the operating condition of most vehicle-scrapping centres?
x: Most vehicle-scrapping centres were operating below 20% of their capacity. The alternatives change the reported level of utilisation and therefore do not reflect the finding of the report.

s: Who launched Bharat Taxi, India's first cooperative ride-hailing platform, on 5 February 2026?
x: Cooperation Minister Amit Shah launched Bharat Taxi; Rekha Gupta was linked to Delhi's partnership with it.

s: Bharat Taxi is described as India's first what?
x: Bharat Taxi is described as the first cooperative ride-hailing platform.

s: Which State/UT became the first to partner with Bharat Taxi?
x: Delhi was first, via an MoU between DTTDC and Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Ltd in the presence of CM Rekha Gupta.

s: What measure did the Union Power Minister direct at the Salal Hydroelectric Project amid the Indus Waters Treaty being in abeyance?
x: The Union Power Minister directed sediment flushing at the Salal Hydroelectric Project. The project began construction in 1970, entered commercial operation in 1987, and provides 12.5% of its power to J&K; these are associated facts, not the directed measure.

s: Who launched National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0, the second phase of asset monetisation of brownfield infrastructure?
x: Nirmala Sitharaman launched National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0. Shivraj Singh Chouhan launched Bharat-VISTAAR, while Amit Shah launched Vibrant Villages Programme-II.

s: What happens to ownership and revenue rights under National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0, which supports the National Infrastructure Pipeline?
o: Ownership remains with the government while revenue rights are leased
Ownership is transferred while the government keeps revenue rights
Both ownership and revenue rights are sold
x: Under NMP 2.0 government ownership is retained while revenue rights are leased.

s: Which group of sectors was covered under the first National Monetisation Pipeline launched in 2021?
o: Roads, railways, power transmission and ports
Roads, railways, power transmission and airports
